To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a knob-associated his-tidine-rich protein N-terminal protein export sequence is required for trafficking of the PfEMP1 C terminus and transmembrane domain to the surface of the infected red blood cell.
the N-terminus of the knob-associated histidine rich protein (KAHRPs) contains the necessary information to export proteins to the outside membrane of the infected red blood cell (IRBC).
we have identified the sequences in P. falciparium that are required to export proteins to the surface of the infected red blood cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the trafficking of the malaria parasite P. falciparam and the proteins that are trafficked.
the trafficking and export of proteins to the surface of the malaria parasite-infected red blood cell.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie malaria parasite biology and the development of novel malaria vaccines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protein export element of the KAHRP protein is sufficient for export of the PfEMP1 protein to the RBC surface.
the protein export element of KAHRP is sufficient to traffic the PfEMP1 protein to the surface of the infected erythrocyte.
PfEMP1 is transported to the surface of P. falciparam-infected RBCs by the parasite's own machinery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the parasite has evolved a mechanism for exporting proteins across three membranes and into the RBC compartment that is distinct from the classical vesicular pathway.
we have shown that the trafficking machinery in the malaria parasite is very similar to the one in the human host, but the parasite has adapted the machinery to export the virulence factor PfEMP1.
the trafficking machinery of P. falcipurum has evolved to be very similar to that of other apicomplexan parasites such as Toxoplasma and Cryptosporidium.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we were able to show that the N-terminal domain of the KAHRP is sufficient for export of a heterologous protein to the surface of P. falciparium-infected erythroicytes, and that this protein export element can be appended to a variety of proteins.

the trafficking of proteins to the infected red cell surface requires the presence of the N-terminal domain of the knob-associated histidine protein (KAHR) and a transmembrane region, but the C-terminal domain is not essential.
PfEMP1 is transported from the parasite to the surface of the infected RBC in an intact complex, and not as a vesicle.
